item.content:encoded:
El mediocampista ingresó al minuto 78 ante Stuttgart y puso fin a casi cinco meses sin actividad oficial con el Atlético de Madrid
La espera terminó para Obed Vargas, quien este martes 20 de octubre disputó sus primeros minutos en la UEFA Champions League con el Atlético de Madrid. El mediocampista mexicano ingresó al minuto 78 en el empate 1-1 ante Stuttgart, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la fase de liga, y consiguió así uno de los principales objetivos de su primera etapa en el futbol europeo.
El ingreso de Vargas ocurrió en un momento complicado para el conjunto de Diego Simeone. Morten Hjulmand había sido expulsado al minuto 64, por lo que el Atlético afrontó los últimos minutos con 10 jugadores y tuvo que modificar su estructura para proteger el empate. El mexicano entró en sustitución de Julián Álvarez y se incorporó al mediocampo dentro de un esquema 5-3-1.
Para Vargas, además, significó el regreso a la actividad después de casi cinco meses sin disputar un partido oficial con el primer equipo rojiblanco, luego de ver minutos en el duelo ante el Valencia de la jornada 34 de LaLiga de España el 2 de mayo de 2026 en el que fue titular y sumó 61′ minutos de juego.
El resultado terminó 1-1 después de que Jamie Leweling adelantara al Stuttgart al minuto 36 y Julián Álvarez empatara al 47. Con este partido, Atlético de Madrid sumó un punto en Alemania y Vargas se convirtió en el mexicano número 31 en registrar minutos en el recuento histórico de la Champions League, después de que Álvaro Fidalgo se incorporara a la lista el pasado 8 de septiembre con el Real Betis.
¿Cómo fue el debut de Obed Vargas en la Champions League?
Simeone recurrió a Vargas cuando el partido había cambiado por completo. El Atlético había encontrado el empate con Álvarez, pero la expulsión de Hjulmand obligó al entrenador argentino a priorizar el equilibrio y la recuperación de espacios. Vargas tuvo la responsabilidad de incorporarse al mediocampo en una fase en la que el Stuttgart tenía la iniciativa y buscaba aprovechar la superioridad numérica.
El mexicano no tuvo tiempo para generar una acción ofensiva determinante. En los minutos que tuvo sobre la cancha buscó participar en el mediocampo, pidió el balón y colaboró con el equipo mientras Stuttgart presionaba en busca del segundo gol. Su actuación dejó algunos números destacados pese al poco tiempo disponible. De acuerdo con las estadísticas tras el encuentro, disputó 12 minutos, completó el 100% de sus pases, recorrió 2.14 kilómetros y alcanzó una velocidad máxima de 33.72 kilómetros por hora, además de no cometer faltas. El equipo terminó replegado durante los últimos minutos y resistió las aproximaciones de los locales para conservar el empate.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: El PSG acaba con la perfección del Barcelona
¿Cuántos mexicanos han disputado la Champions League?
Con el ingreso de Obed Vargas, 31 futbolistas con nacionalidad mexicana han registrado minutos en la máxima competencia europea. El anterior a la lista en incorporarse había sido Álvaro Fidalgo, quien debutó con el Real Betis ante Lille el 8 de septiembre.
La lista reúne a varias generaciones de futbolistas mexicanos que han participado con clubes de España, Inglaterra, Alemania, Portugal, Países Bajos, Italia, Grecia y Francia. Entre ellos destacan Héctor Herrera, Javier ‘Chicharito’ Hernández y Rafael Márquez, quienes encabezan el registro de apariciones con 52, 46 y 45 partidos, respectivamente, según los datos de Transfermarkt.
Los 31 mexicanos que han disputado la Champions League
La historia cronológica de los futbolistas mexicanos en la máxima competición europea comenzó bajo el antiguo formato de la Copa de Europa, antecesora de la actual Champions League. El 17 de septiembre de 1986, Hugo Sánchez disputó su primer partido con el Real Madrid ante el Young Boys, en un encuentro que terminó con derrota 1-0 para el conjunto español. El delantero mexicano marcó en el partido de vuelta, el 1 de octubre, durante la victoria 5-0 del Madrid.
Tuvieron que pasar 14 años para el siguiente debut mexicano, protagonizado por Rafael Márquez con el Mónaco el 12 de septiembre de 2000, en la derrota 3-2 ante Galatasaray. El defensa michoacano disputó los 90 minutos y comenzó así una trayectoria europea que posteriormente lo llevaría al Barcelona, donde se convirtió en el primer mexicano en ganar la Champions League.
La siguiente generación comenzó a aparecer poco después. Sergio Almaguer se estrenó en 2002 con el Galatasaray, mientras que Nery Castillo lo hizo en 2003 con el Olympiacos. Después llegaron Carlos Salcido y Francisco “Kikín” Fonseca en 2006, antes de que Pável Pardo, Ricardo Osorio y Giovani dos Santos coincidieran en la misma jornada del 19 de septiembre de 2007. Pardo y Osorio fueron titulares con el Stuttgart ante Rangers, mientras Giovani ingresó como suplente en el triunfo 3-0 del Barcelona sobre Lyon. UEFA registra a los dos mexicanos del Stuttgart como titulares y a Giovani como sustituto de Xavi Hernández.
La década de 2010 trajo la llegada de una nueva generación de referentes. Javier ‘Chicharito’ Hernández debutó con Manchester United el 14 de septiembre de 2010, como titular ante Rangers y con participación durante los 90 minutos. Posteriormente aparecieron Héctor Herrera en 2013, Raúl Jiménez en 2014 y la dupla mexicana del Porto formada por Jesús ‘Tecatito’ Corona y Miguel Layún en 2015. En el caso de Corona y Layún, ambos participaron en el partido que Porto empató 2-2 ante Dynamo Kyiv el 16 de septiembre de 2015; Layún fue titular y Corona ingresó en el segundo tiempo.
A esa generación se sumaron Hirving ‘Chucky’ Lozano en 2018 y Edson Álvarez en 2019. Lozano comenzó su recorrido en la Champions con el PSV Eindhoven ante Barcelona el 18 de septiembre de 2018, mientras que Álvarez hizo lo propio un año después con el Ajax frente al Lille. El mexicano, además, marcó un gol en su debut, un hecho que el propio Ajax destacó como la primera anotación de un mexicano en su estreno en la competición.
La etapa más reciente comenzó con Santiago Giménez el 25 de octubre de 2023, cuando el delantero marcó un doblete en la victoria 3-1 del Feyenoord sobre la Lazio. UEFA registró aquella actuación como una de las principales historias de la tercera jornada de la competición.
La nueva generación continuó con Rodrigo Huescas, quien disputó su primer partido de Champions el 20 de agosto de 2025, con el FC Copenhagen ante Basel durante la fase de clasificación. Posteriormente llegaron Álvaro Fidalgo, quien debutó con el Real Betis el 8 de septiembre de 2026, y Obed Vargas, quien se estrenó con el Atlético de Madrid en octubre de 2026. Con su aparición, Vargas se convirtió en el mexicano número 31 en disputar la competición.
Héctor Herrera encabeza el historial mexicano en Champions
Héctor Herrera es el mexicano con más apariciones en la competición, con 52 partidos, seguido por Javier Hernández con 46 y Rafael Márquez con 45. Jesús ‘Tecatito’ Corona aparece también entre los principales representantes mexicanos, con 41 encuentros según el recuento de UEFA.
Rafael Márquez conserva además una distinción particular dentro de la historia mexicana en el torneo: conquistó la Champions League en dos ocasiones con Barcelona, en 2006 y 2009. Jonathan dos Santos también formó parte del Barcelona campeón de 2011 y disputó minutos durante aquella edición.
¿Qué mexicanos han estado en clubes de Champions pero no han debutado?
La lista de futbolistas mexicanos relacionados con la Champions es más amplia si se consideran quienes estuvieron vinculados o registrados con clubes participantes, pero nunca sumaron minutos. Antes del estreno de Vargas, seis casos se destacan: Alan Pulido con Olympiacos, Rogelio Funes Mori con Benfica, Eugenio Pizzuto con Lille, Álex Padilla con Athletic Club, Stéphano Carrillo con Feyenoord y el propio Obed con Atlético de Madrid. La diferencia entre estar registrado o convocado y realmente jugar un partido es la que determina la inclusión en el listado de 31.
Para Obed Vargas, la noche en Stuttgart representa el comienzo de una nueva etapa. El mexicano ya tiene sus primeros minutos en Champions League, su nombre quedó inscrito junto al de 30 compatriotas que lo precedieron y ahora buscará que esta primera aparición con el Atlético de Madrid sea el punto de partida para conseguir más oportunidades bajo las órdenes de Diego Simeone.

Early voting push ramps up amid ballot-counting legal battle
The Trump administration is asking a judge to pause the counting of mail-in ballots from alleged noncitizens in California until their immigration status can be verified.
The race is on to get out the vote in the final stretch of the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.
President Donald Trump continued his campaign travel blitz on Saturday with a rally in Kentucky aimed at boosting Republican turnout.
Meanwhile, organizers planned hundreds of "No Kings" rallies across the country this weekend. Many attendees held signs opposing Trump's policies, but organizers framed the events as a nonpartisan effort to encourage early voting. The national movement is also mobilizing to prepare for "mass nonviolent action in rapid response to election disruption or subversion if needed."
The rallies come amid an escalating legal battle in California, where the Trump administration is asking a judge to pause the counting of mail-in ballots from suspected noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed as part of a broader effort to prevent fraud.
California's Secretary of State Shirley Weber says the federal government hasn't provided evidence to support its allegations and warns that these "unprecedented measures" could threaten voting rights.
The Justice Department upped the stakes, warning in a letter addressed to the Los Angeles County Counsel’s office that local election officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters may be at risk of prosecution.
"They will all go to jail for a long period of time," Trump said on social media.
Meanwhile, Democratic Senators Alex Padilla, Dick Durbin and Sheldon Whitehouse are urging the Justice Department in a letter to reaffirm that it won't interfere in the election and rule out any attempt to seize ballots before the midterm results are certified.
The DOJ didn't immediately respond to requests for comment on the letter.

No Kings rallies across US urge voters to cast ballots early ahead of midterms
Rallies organized by the No Kings network opposed to President Donald Trump were held Saturday in cities and communities across the U.S., with an aim of getting people out to vote early in the midterm elections.
The hundreds of planned events were billed as nonpartisan, though they sought to build on nearly two years’ worth of No Kings marches and demonstrations by people upset with Trump’s presidency.
A band entertained what appeared to be a few hundred people in caps and coats at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington. Despite the chilly weather, many in the crowd danced to the tunes. “VOTE EARLY” and “HANDS OFF MY VOTE!” were among the many signs held aloft.
At an Atlanta rally, City Councilman Michael Julian Bond told the crowd to urge others to vote ahead of the Nov. 3 general election.
“The Constitution gives you one power, right? That is the power to vote. Are you gonna use that power?” he said.
“You don’t see Superman giving up his power,” Bond continued. “You don’t see Black Panther giving up his power. You don’t see Wonder Woman giving up her magic lasso. So why would you give up your right, your power, your obligation to vote? Be a super hero, use your power. Go to the polls and vote.”
Trump has long been suspicious of mail voting and has claimed without evidence that voting fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election.
His administration sued California election officials Thursday, asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots for the midterm elections from people whom the federal government has identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed.
On Friday the Justice Department warned that local officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation and potential prosecution.
Earlier that day Democratic Sens. Alex Padilla of California, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island and Dick Durbin of Illinois wrote to Attorney General Todd Blanche demanding that the Justice Department commit to not seizing ballots or other election materials before the midterm elections are certified.

Johan Vasquez y César Montes completaron los 90 minutos en la derrota del Genoa y el Lokomotiv, de manera respectiva, en la actividad de los mexicanos este sábado en el futbol de Europa.
Murallas mexicanas
El capitán Johan Vásquez que fue titular, jugó todo el partido y se ganó una tarjeta amarilla al minuto 51, en la derrota del Genoa ante la Roma con un marcador 2-0 en la Serie A.
Por su parte, el Cachorro Montes disputó los 90 minutos en un partidazo con marcador 3-3 del Lokomotiv Moscú en contra del Krasnodar.
Al defensor mexicano le mostraron la tarjeta amarilla a los 2 minutos de haber iniciado el encuentro.
Poca actividad mexicana en La Liga
El Valencia, dirigido por Javier “Vasco” Aguirre, consiguió un punto en el empate sin goles contra el Athletic Club.
El Vasco sigue sin ganar desde su llegada al Valencia, que se ubica en la penúltima posición de la tabla con apenas seis puntos.
Mientras, el portero Alex Padilla se mantuvo en la banca en el mismo partido de la jornada 9. El mexicano sigue a la espera de una oportunidad de defender el arco.
Por su parte, Álvaro Fidalgo vio minutos en la goleada 5-2 que recibió el Betis a domicilio por parte del FC Barcelona.
El mediocampista que jugó el Mundial 2026 ingresó a la cancha al minuto 69 en lo que ya era un partido resuelto.
A su vez, Obed Vargas sigue sin sumar minutos con el Atlético de Madrid, pues se quedó en el banco de suplentes en el triunfo 1-0 sobre Espanyol.
Actividad de los mexicanos de Europa en domingo
Se espera que el domingo Luis Chávez, Armando “Hormiga” González, Mateo Chávez y Rodrigo Huescas tengan actividad con sus respectivos equipos.
El Dinamo de Moscú, donde milita Chávez, se medirá ante el CSKA de Moscú en el que promete ser un partido emocionante.
Ambos equipos buscan la cima de la Liga Premier de Rusia y se espera que el mexicano sume minutos.
Mateo Chávez busca mantenerse como figura del AZ Alkmaar en el partido en contra del Cambuur, en busca de puntos para alcanzar al Feyenoord en la lucha por la Eredivisie.
Rodrigo Huescas quiere ser relevante con el Copenhague para mantener a su equipo como líder de la Superliga danesa cuando enfrente al Aarhus GF, que necesita salir de la zona de descenso.
Y la Hormiga González quiere volver a su mejor versión y necesita marcar con el Olympiacos en el partido de mañana, en el que visitan al Panetolikos en la Super Liga de Grecia.

item.content:encoded:
At least 9 California federal lawmakers targeted in nationwide mail threat
- Click here to listen to this article
At least nine federal lawmakers from California, including Sen. Alex Padilla, are among the dozens of elected officials and state election offices nationwide that have received suspicious letters containing a white powdery substance, prompting police responses and evacuations.
The letters, which preliminary tests so far indicate do not contain a hazardous material, have been sent to both Democrat and Republican lawmakers, including California Reps. Gil Cisneros (D-Covina); Jimmy Panetta (D-Carmel Valley Village) and Kevin Kiley (R-Rocklin), among others.
Delivered just weeks before the hotly contested Nov. 3 general election, the letters have drawn bipartisan condemnation.
Kiley said Friday that one of his staff members opened an envelope containing the substance and immediately placed it in a quarantine enclosure designed for such an incident. It prompted a response by the Roseville Fire Hazmat Task Force, and there were no reports of injuries.
“This incident highlights — once again — why we need to bring down the temperature in our politics and embrace a return to civility and common sense,” Kiley posted on X.
Panetta said an envelope containing the powder was delivered to his Santa Cruz district office and opened by a staff member, prompting the office to be evacuated, with staff later cleared by medical personnel.
“Threats, fear-mongering, and violence against public servants have become far too common over the past decade and undermine our democracy,” Panetta said. “But these attempts to intimidate us will not deter us from doing our job.”
The nationwide incidents have prompted an investigation by the FBI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service and U.S. Capitol Police, which was disclosed Thursday in a message from the Senate Sergeant at Arms. It said that law enforcement officials were working to intercept any additional letters, but “it is possible that some letters may reach their destinations.”
On Saturday, the FBI said it was continuing to work “with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident” and identify the responsible parties.
The recipients of the letters include national figures, including Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz, whose Houston office reportedly received a letter Friday afternoon prompting a lockdown, and former presidential candidate Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), who posted on X that the letter was sent to her state office but intercepted by postal workers.
Padilla said postal inspectors intercepted a suspicious parcel addressed to his office, according to reports. He could not be reached for comment Saturday.
State election offices in Alabama, Arizona, Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Washington, Wisconsin and Wyoming have also received packages as of Friday afternoon, NBC reported.
The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors issued a joint statement condemning what they said were threats against election staff.
“Those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties,” they said.
This is not the first time suspicious packages have been sent to elected officials prior to an election. In 2024, at least six secretaries of state offices received threatening letters containing suspicious substances, though hazardous material was not found, according to media reports.
There was also a similar threat in 2023 when election offices in California, Georgia, Nevada, Oregon and Washington state received mailings that contained a white powder, some of which contained traces of the powerful opioid fentanyl, NBC reported.
The other California lawmakers who issued statements that they were sent letters this week were Rep. Zoe Lofgren (D-San Jose), Rep. Ami Bera (D-Elk Grove) and Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-Concord). Rep. Josh Harder (D-Tracy) also reportedly received a letter.
With widespread reports about the letter circulating among elected officials, a staff member of DeSaulnier’s Walnut Creek office noticed a letter matching the description and return address on Friday afternoon and called law enforcement without opening it, the lawmaker posted on X.
“Threats and political violence seem to have reached a fever pitch in our country, and I urge my fellow Americans to stand united against such attempts at undermining our democracy,” he said in the post.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
This story was originally published by The Merced FOCUS.
It’s salmon squeezing time at California’s newest, most technologically advanced fish hatchery.
Standing in a large tank filled with 54 degree water, a fish technician passes an ultrasound wand across the abdomen of an adult female Chinook salmon to ensure its eggs are fully developed.
If so, techs then squeeze out some eggs from the salmon’s belly while feeling for the looseness of the remaining eggs. Each ripe female is then transported into a separate holding tank for spawning the following day.
Male broodstock get similar handling, except the squeezing is employed to express milt. The males also get scanned (via a transponder tag embedded in their abdomen) to determine which are the least genetically related to the females.
Why? Because the last thing biologists want, especially when resurrecting a salmon run that was killed off for more than six decades, is inbred fish.
“Genetic diversity is really important in a population because it gives the population the ability to adapt to changing conditions in the river,” explained Brian Erlandsen, a senior environmental scientist supervisor for the California Department of Fish and Wildlife. “So you try to maximize that as much as you can.”
Opened in May 2025 along the San Joaquin River in the town of Friant, just outside Fresno, the Salmon Conservation and Research Facility produces spring-run Chinook salmon expressly for the San Joaquin River Restoration Program.
Made up of five federal and state government agencies, the Friant Water Users Authority, exchange contractors and environmental organizations, the San Joaquin River Restoration Program (SJRRP) is the result of a 2006 legal settlement that followed an 18-year lawsuit over California’s second-longest river.
Its purpose: To bring back a once-mighty salmon run, the southernmost in the state, which went belly up when the completion of Friant Dam in 1942 virtually dried up a 150-mile stretch of the San Joaquin River from the dam down to the Merced River confluence.
Salmon are anadromous fish, meaning they live in both fresh and salt water and travel up and down river systems during their life cycle. Born in fresh water, juveniles migrate to the ocean to mature then return as adults to their native streams to spawn and die.
A robust salmon run
Before Friant Dam, an estimated 200,000 to 500,000 adult Chinook salmon returned to the San Joaquin River each year. The runs were said to be so dense that inhabitants who lived nearby were kept awake at night by the sound of fish splashing their way upstream.
Today, the only evidence of this former abundance exists in old photographs such as those displayed at Scout Island in northwest Fresno.
“People used to pitchfork the salmon, fill up barges with fish and bring them down the river to San Francisco and sell them in the fish market,” said Don Portz, a Bureau of Reclamation fish biologist who serves as SJRRP program manager. “I mean just crazy stuff.”
The SJRRP operates under two co-equal goals designed to balance ecological recovery with regional economic stability: Restore and maintain a self-sustaining population of spring-run Chinook salmon — but do so in a manner that does not adversely impact farmers that rely on water from the river and stored in Millerton Lake.
Due to a variety of factors, not the least of which were severe droughts from 2007-09, 2012-16 and 2020-22 that reduced recovery flows in the river, program managers are well behind the timeline established by the 2006 settlement.
Still, there has been progress. The SJRRP reached a milestone in the summer of 2025 when 448 adult spring-run Chinook salmon returned to the river — the highest number by far since juveniles were first reintroduced in 2014.
Most of those 448 returning adults were released as juveniles in 2023 and likely benefitted from high flows caused by flood releases from Friant Dam during their out-migration period, CDFW spokesperson Krysten Kellum said. This year, by comparison, just 54 adult salmon returned to the river out of the roughly 220,000 juveniles released in 2024’s drier conditions.
Blockages impede salmon
Despite increased flows mandated by the settlement, salmon are prevented by structural blockages from swimming unencumbered up and down the river system.
Each early spring, juvenile salmon raised at the $44 million state bond-funded hatchery are transported by truck and released at the Merced River confluence near Newman.
The Salmon Conservation and Research Facility will produce roughly 250,000 juveniles for release next spring but has capacity for up to 1 million. In summer, returning adults are captured in long, cylindrical nets at multiple locations and trucked to Fresno, where they swim upriver to spawning beds below the dam.
To allow the fish to migrate freely along a river system that has been altered significantly since historical times, four major passage impediment projects must be completed.
The first is currently underway east of Dos Palos. Construction of a bypass channel that will reroute the river around Sack Dam and the Arroyo Canal began in 2025. When finished, adult salmon will be able to swim upstream via a ladder and ramp during normal and higher flows while juveniles moving downstream will be able to pass through a control structure.
The Bureau of Reclamation awarded a $93 million contract for that project but actual costs could exceed $100 million, Portz said.
“What we are doing out there is truly an amazing feat,” Portz added. “If you look at the size of that project alone, I don't know of another project in California of that size that is for water conveyance and fisheries protection in one lump.”
A significantly larger amount of federal funding — perhaps as much as $700 million — will be required near Mendota, where there are plans to build a half-mile channel around Mendota Pool with levees capable of withstanding flood-level flows. Other components include a fish ladder and screen, reverse flow facility, a fish recapture facility and a new south-end dam.
Senator requests extra $500 million
To fully fund the Mendota Pool bypass project, Senator Alex Padilla (D-California) introduced a bill that would allocate an additional $500 million to the SJRRP. The Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources advanced the bill in July; it awaits a full floor vote.
Work on the Mendota Pool bypass is expected to begin in 2028, Portz said, following completion of the Sack Dam and Arroyo Canal project.
The two other passage impediment projects, improving fish passages at the Eastside Bypass Control Structure and Chowchilla Bifurcation, are purview of the California Department of Water Resources. Funding for both has been approved.
Other factors that have hampered salmon restoration efforts include low flows during drought years and, to a lesser extent, seepage into adjacent orchards and predation by bass and other nonnative fish.
Portz, who has managed the SJRPP since 2018, estimated it would take until 2035 for the river system to be completely navigable by salmon during normal and wet years. Which, he acknowledged, is well outside the timeline contained in the 2006 settlement. Restoration flows were supposed to have occurred by 2014.
“However, if you took and you truly look at what it takes to bring back a river from a dry, sandy, barren river channel to reconstituting water and bringing back an extirpated species, I’d say we're doing pretty darn good right now and gaining steam,” Portz said.

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Federal investigators are working to identify who sent dozens of suspicious letters to election offices and elected officials across the country, including one addressed to the Georgia Secretary of State’s Office.
The FBI intercepted a letter intended for Georgia’s Secretary of State as part of a larger investigation involving election offices in at least 15 states.
Some of the letters contained an unknown substance, prompting federal authorities to warn congressional and election offices to treat the mailings as “potentially hazardous.”
Retired FBI Atlanta Special Agent Marc Benjamin says investigators will carefully examine the letters for evidence that could help identify the sender.
“Looking for evidence to include fingerprints, DNA, perhaps type setting,” Benjamin said.
Benjamin says the FBI’s Evidence Response Team will also work to determine what substances may be inside the envelopes.
“The FBI will absolutely send out the ERT, the Evidence Response Team, to collect and isolate the letters; and then try to identify whatever suspicious substance could be contained within those letters,” Benjamin said.
The investigation extends beyond election offices. Several Democratic senators, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and California Sen. Alex Padilla, were also targeted. Officials say no U.S. House representatives were targeted.
Federal authorities say they are continuing to intercept additional letters before they reach their intended destinations.
The mailings come as early and absentee voting continues ahead of the November midterm elections.
“In addition to any immediate risk of threat the letters may pose, the other risk is the disruption to the election process,” Benjamin said.
Benjamin says the FBI will work with law enforcement agencies nationwide to alert political offices about the suspicious mailings and help prevent further incidents.
The investigation follows a similar situation in 2023, when the Fulton County Elections Office and election workers in several other states received letters containing powdery substances.
The FBI continues working with law enforcement partners to identify those responsible for the latest mailings across the country.
WSB Radio’s Ashley Simmons & Jonathan O’Brien contributed to this story.

By Steve Neavling
Federal law enforcement agencies are investigating a series of letters containing suspicious substances that were mailed to congressional offices and election officials across the country, prompting warnings that the packages should be treated as potentially dangerous.
The FBI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service and U.S. Capitol Police are working to intercept additional letters, according to a Senate Sergeant at Arms notice obtained by The Associated Press. The warning said that while authorities are trying to stop the mailings before delivery, “it is possible that some letters may reach their destinations.”
Several Democratic senators were among those targeted. Capitol Police intercepted a letter containing a “suspicious substance” that was sent to Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware, while suspicious mail addressed to Sens. Alex Padilla of California and Kirsten Gillibrand of New York was intercepted by postal inspectors before reaching their offices.
Election offices have also received suspicious packages. Mail containing powdery substances led to evacuations in Louisiana and Oklahoma, while election officials in Ohio, Wisconsin and several other states reported receiving letters or having them intercepted. Wisconsin officials said testing showed the white powder sent there was not hazardous.
“Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,” Wisconsin elections administrator Meagan Wolfe said.
The mailings come about three weeks before Election Day and resemble a series of threats in 2023, when election offices in six states received letters containing white powder, including some with traces of fentanyl.
“Those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties,” the National Association of Secretaries of State and National Association of State Election Directors said in a joint statement.

item.content:encoded:
Federal investigators are tracing a wave of suspicious letters sent to senators, state election offices and other recipients across the US, some of them containing an unidentified powder.
More than 100 letters were mailed nationwide, according to officials briefed on the investigation, and offices in Louisiana and Arizona were partly evacuated.
News of the nationwide mailings emerged on Thursday 15 October 2026, 25 years to the day after a staff member in a Senate office opened a letter laced with anthrax. No injuries had been reported as of Thursday.
Senators and More Than a Dozen States Targeted
The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service are investigating 'a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices', the FBI said.
'Some of the letters contained an unknown substance and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident,' it added, Votebeat reported.
A notice from the Senate sergeant-at-arms warned of 'multiple letters containing suspicious substances that were mailed to various addresses nationwide' and said law enforcement was 'working to intercept any additional letters before they are delivered', Roll Call reported.
One of Senator Chris Murphy's state offices in Connecticut received a letter, and his spokesman said the senator and his staff 'were not in immediate danger'. A letter addressed to Senator Alex Padilla's office was intercepted by the Postal Service. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer was also among those targeted.
The senators identified in these reports are Democrats, although the full list of recipients has not been made public, and no motive has been disclosed.
The House sergeant-at-arms said that 'no House Members have been identified as intended recipients at this time'. US Capitol Police referred questions to the FBI. Three officials briefed on the investigation told Votebeat that the recipients also included a polling organisation, and that it was not yet clear how many letters went to election officials.
Evacuations and Intercepted Mail
In Louisiana, an employee in the Secretary of State's elections division opened a package at about 12.20pm on Tuesday 13 October and found an unknown white powder, WAFB reported. 'Out of an abundance of caution, we have evacuated the Elections section and turned off the building's air conditioning,' Secretary of State Nancy Landry said. The office reopened on Wednesday after officials found no harmful substance.
In Arizona, staff in Secretary of State Adrian Fontes's office opened an envelope containing white powder on Thursday. Officials isolated those exposed and evacuated other employees while hazardous materials crews cleared the area. Investigators have not said whether the Arizona letter is linked to the others.
'This is a sobering moment that highlights the reality of election administration in this country today,' Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes said on X. 'We will not be scared out of doing our jobs on behalf of the voters of Arizona.'
Oklahoma also reported receiving a letter with a powdery white substance. The Wisconsin Elections Commission received a suspicious mail piece that was later 'deemed not dangerous'. 'Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,' said administrator Meagan Wolfe, adding that it would not affect the general election.
In Nebraska, staff did not open an envelope and handed it to the FBI. 'In both instances, swift action was taken to isolate and then investigate the suspicious mailing,' said Secretary of State Bob Evnen, whose office had received a similar envelope in 2024.
Other letters never reached their targets. Law enforcement intercepted letters bound for election offices in Ohio, New Hampshire, Washington, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Georgia, Idaho and South Dakota.
Pennsylvania's Department of State said the Postal Service blocked delivery of a suspicious letter on Wednesday, and the FBI field office in Connecticut said it had 'received multiple interceptions'.
'Election officials should never have to fear for their personal safety while performing their duties,' said Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose.
Twenty-Five Years After the Anthrax Letters
The timing carried an unsettling echo. On 15 October 2001, a staff member in the office of then-Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle opened a letter in the Hart Senate Office Building that appeared to come from a fourth-grade class, and white powder spilled out. It was anthrax.
The 2001 attacks, which also targeted news organisations and included a letter addressed to Senator Patrick Leahy, killed five people and sickened 17 others. The Hart building underwent extensive decontamination.
The FBI later concluded that Bruce Ivins, a scientist at a US Army biodefence laboratory, was responsible. Ivins died in 2008 before charges could be filed, and the investigation was formally closed in 2010. The FBI's conclusion was never tested in court, and a National Academy of Sciences review later questioned aspects of the scientific evidence.
Mail for Congress is now processed and screened offsite, a safeguard introduced after the attacks, Roll Call reported.
Election offices have faced similar scares before. In 2024, election officials in at least six states received suspicious packages, according to CNN reporting cited by Votebeat, and Nebraska received its first such envelope that year.
Investigators have not publicly identified who sent the latest letters or established whether the timing was deliberate. The FBI said it could not confirm details of specific cases.
The mailings come less than three weeks before the 3 November midterm elections.

item.dc:creator: David Prior

States including Louisiana, Ohio, and Oklahoma have been identified among those whose election offices received the suspicious correspondence. A spokesperson for the Louisiana Se…
item.content:encoded:
Federal authorities are actively investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to state election officials and congressional offices across multiple states.
The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service confirmed the probe, with some of the mailings reported to contain a powdery white substance of unknown composition.
States including Louisiana, Ohio, and Oklahoma have been identified among those whose election offices received the suspicious correspondence.
A spokesperson for the Louisiana Secretary of State, Trey Williams, confirmed that an employee who opened a letter on Tuesday was taken to the emergency room as a precaution, though law enforcement found no evidence of harmful substances.
Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., confirmed his office was among those targeted, noting that the U.S. Postal Service intercepted a suspicious package before it reached his staff.
“Thankfully, no threat was posed to my staff or our office,” Padilla said in a statement to NPR.
Padilla added that “this incident is a stark reminder of the very real dangers facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections in the face of increasingly hostile political rhetoric — especially from Donald Trump.”
Deputy Chief Inspector Brendan Donahue of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service confirmed that authorities were able to stop delivery of at least one of the mailings before it reached its destination.
“Some of the letters have contained an unknown substance, and we’re working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident,” Donahue said.
A communication from the Senate’s Sergeant at Arms to congressional staff warned that suspicious letters could be identified by discoloration, powder emanating from envelopes, and postmarks that do not match the return address.
An image included in that communication showed a return address labeled “DSA” with a New York City return address listed on the envelope.
Staff were instructed that all suspicious letters, packages, or substances “should be treated as potentially hazardous and handled in accordance with established safety protocols.”
The FBI stated it is “working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters,” as the investigation spans multiple jurisdictions nationwide.
The incidents echo similar events in 2024, when more than 15 state election offices across the country received suspicious mailings in a comparable pattern.
With less than three weeks remaining until the November 3 midterm elections, the National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors issued a joint statement asserting that “those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties.”

item.content:encoded:
This initiative would change California’s constitution to require voters to provide a government-issued ID when they cast a ballot. Mail-in voters would have to include the last four digits of their ID on the ballot envelope. The measure would also require election officials to use “best efforts,” using government data to verify that voters on registration rolls are U.S. citizens, and to report annually the percentage verified.
What’s at stake?
Voter ID. This would be a big change from how voting currently works in California.
Right now, election officials verify a voter’s identity when they register to vote. They also verify that the signature on a voter’s mail-in ballot matches the signature in their voter registration file.
But voters do not have to provide ID every time they cast a ballot.
Prop. 39 would change that and require voters to present a government-issued ID every time they vote.
The initiative would also shrink the long list of documents the state currently accepts as proof of identity and residency for voting purposes. If Prop. 39 passes, only government-issued IDs, such as a driver’s license, passport, or state ID card, would be accepted.
The measure would require California to offer free state ID cards to eligible voters who lack another type of government-issued ID.
Official title on the ballot: Prop. 39: Prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification
Language you will see:
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements.

What your vote means
- A "yes" vote means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
- A "no" vote means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
Understanding Prop. 39
Currently, when someone registers to vote in California, they do not have to provide proof of citizenship. Rather, they have to check a box on their registration form attesting to being a U.S. citizen and California resident.
Lying on that form is a crime (perjury) punishable by fines and jail time.
Prop. 39 wouldn’t change that process.
What it would do is require election officials to make “best efforts” to verify the citizenship of people on voter registration rolls by cross-referencing their information against government data.
Why now?
According to a recent UC Berkeley poll, just 22% of California Republicans surveyed have confidence in the election system, compared to 88% of Democrats. The two Republican legislators who proposed Prop. 39 see it as a step toward remedying that distrust.
President Donald Trump has also increasingly cast doubt on the integrity of elections across the U.S., including the claim that large numbers of noncitizens are voting. Efforts to find and prosecute noncitizen voters have thus far turned up few culprits.
But there have been a handful of recent cases in the news of noncitizens registering to vote, including a Honduran green card-holder who was charged with voter fraud in August. Last year, an election integrity activist in Orange County was charged with fraud for registering and voting for her dog.
Here’s what supporters say
- Supporters of Prop. 39 say requiring voter ID is a common sense reform to increase trust in the electoral process while maintaining voter conveniences including mail-in ballots. Supporters note that polling has found widespread support for voter ID across political parties. They also say using a voter’s signature on their mail-in ballot to verify identity, as California currently does, delays election results and causes some valid voters to have their ballots rejected.
- Notable supporters: California Republican Party, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton, U.S. Congressman Ken Calvert (CA-41), Republican state Senator. Tony Strickland (Huntington Beach), Republican Assemblymember Carl DeMaio (San Diego).
Here’s what opponents say
- Opponents of Prop. 39 note that documented voter fraud is extremely rare. They say the initiative feeds into Trump’s false claims of widespread election fraud, and would unfairly shut out eligible voters who make simple mistakes, like mixing up their ID number when writing it on their ballot envelope. They also say the federal government’s current system for verifying state voters’ eligibility is prone to error. 
- Notable opposition: California Democratic Party, UCLA Voting Rights Project, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla, California Labor Federation
Potential financial impact
The state Legislative Analyst’s Office estimates that implementing Prop. 39 could cost anywhere from tens of millions to several hundred million dollars. Read the full analysis here.
What it takes to win
A majority is needed to pass.

WATCH: Padilla Slams Trump DOJ Attempts to Interfere in California Elections
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) joined CNN’s In the Arena with Kasie Hunt to blast the Trump Administration’s baseless lawsuit to interfere in California’s 2026 midterm election.
Key Excerpts:
On the DOJ’s Lawsuit
The Administration is clearly without any authority, by the way, trying to interfere with the elections. I mean, the department’s own policy is to not engage within 60 days of an election or 19 days out… They’re desperate. They’re looking for this proof that Trump has been barking about for more than ten years about massive voter fraud, which simply does not exist. Now to the why this close to the election? They see the same polls that you guys have been talking about for days and weeks now. They’re walking into a horrible midterm election cycle where voters, voters will hold Trump and Republicans accountable for their horrible record of the last two years. Their only hope for trying to maintain any sense of power is to interfere. It’s to change the rules. It’s to rig the elections. That’s why they’re doing this.
On California’s Election Security
Number one, California does verify a voter’s eligibility on the front end, not when you go vote, but when you first immediately register. Number two, our system, by the way of automatic registration through the Department of Motor Vehicles in California, has provided the most accurate voter rolls we’ve ever had because on a regular basis, people are renewing their driver’s license or their IDs. Once again verifying their information.
But you have to wonder, you know, this thumb drive that appeared in the mail in Los Angeles County? Where did it come from? The database. The list of voters they are suggesting. How did they arrive at that list? We’ve known that the SAVE database, that the Department of Homeland Security has tried to use before for this purpose, is inaccurate. They acknowledge there’s a large false positives here that’s been the result of other states that have tried to utilize it. And again, why this close to the election? They could have had this conversation months and months ago.
[…]
I know how California elections work very, very well. They’re safe, they’re secure. They’re fair, they’re free, and they’re going to stay that way.

item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, released the following statement after the U.S. Department of Justice sued California’s Secretary of State and Los Angeles County’s Registrar Recorder to prevent them from calculating ballots sent to a list of alleged ineligible voters without any legal basis or supporting evidence:
“We’ve seen this coming: Donald Trump’s Department of Justice with no authority is now actively trying to interfere in the 2026 elections and strong-arm California into purging names from our voter rolls and blocking mail ballots based purely on vague allegations less than three weeks before Election Day. This lawsuit has no legal basis or evidence behind it and is nothing more than a blatant abuse of power designed to sow distrust in our elections and threaten Americans’ right to vote. The truth is simple: our elections are safe and secure; the widespread voter fraud that Trump has claimed for 10 years does not exist.
“We will fight this illegal overreach every step of the way.”

Los futbolistas y entrenadores mexicanos en el extranjero tendrán actividad este fin de semana, con partidos importantes en Europa y Arabia Saudita. Senate Democrats announce recruitment of 100+ staffers for election observer program
HUNT VALLEY, Md. (TNND) — Senate Democrats have recruited more than a hundred staffers to act as election observers for the November midterms, Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Senator Alex Padilla announced Wednesday.
The workers, who will travel to polling sites across nine states, are trained to document attempts to interfere with voters, threaten election employees and spread false information on November 3rd and in the following weeks. Schumer and Padilla, the top Democrat on the committee settling contested elections, are promoting their program as a deterrent to the denialism practiced by some Republicans.
“Donald Trump is trying to steal the election – but Democrats and the American people won’t let him,” Schumer said in a statement.
“Our elections are free and secure, but we cannot take that for granted. I am grateful for the Senate staff members who are raising their hand to help build trust in our upcoming election and protect the sanctity of our democracy.”
Trump, who still falsely claims he won his 2020 White House bid, has spent years undermining the security of elections he and his party are positioned to lose. Congressional Republicans, in lockstep with the president, translate his comments to legislative text in the name of voter safeguards.
“If we can get proof of citizenship and photo ID to vote, that eliminates so much of the problem, all the fraud and everything that everybody’s concerned about in our elections, particularly, frankly, in these blue states,” House Speaker Mike Johnson said in July, as Trump pushed Congress to send him the SAVE America Act.
Studies show noncitizen voting is rare and that American elections are secure. The Census Bureau found in August, for example, that of the 128 million records it reviewed in a 2020 election analysis, only 24,000 indicated noncitizen voting.
“The SAVE Act is a solution in search of a problem,” Elaine Kamarck, a fellow at The Brookings Institution, said this past summer. “A minuscule number of noncitizens register to vote, and even fewer manage to vote. Adding extra documentary proof to the registration process will only suppress the vote of people who are under resourced."
The SAVE America Act could reduce Democratic turnout, but Republicans would still face an uphill challenge in keeping their congressional majorities. Trump is dragging down candidates in purple and red states upset with his economic and foreign policies, giving Democrats an opening to take control of the Capitol with messaging centered on change.

item.content:encoded:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) and Senate Committee on Rules and Administration Ranking Member Alex Padilla (D-CA) announced Senate Democrats recruited and trained more than 100 staffers to monitor voting and ballot counting during the upcoming midterm elections.
The official congressional election observers will be deployed to polling sites across nine states with closely contested Senate races in November, Schumer and Padilla told reporters on Wednesday.
“Donald Trump has made clear that he wants to ‘take over the voting’ in state-run elections. Election interference is unconstitutional and illegal and Congress will be watching,” Padilla said.
The announcement comes just 20 days ahead of Election Day, as the Trump administration attempts to disrupt election administration and right-wing activists urge the president to take drastic action to influence the outcome.
Democrats mentioned Ohio, Georgia and Michigan — three states with critical Senate races — as among the states to which monitors would be deployed.
For years now, President Donald Trump has relentlessly sowed doubt in the integrity of U.S. elections.
Attorney General Todd Blanche has said that the Department of Justice plans to send 1,000 election monitors to polling places on Nov. 3.
Trump’s allies have also called for him to send federal immigration enforcement officers to polling places. Department of Homeland Security officials say they don’t plan to send agents en masse to patrol the polls, but various administration officials have evaded attempts by members of Congress to pin them down on the topic.
The president has also tried to implement restrictions on mail-in ballots ahead of the November elections. The Supreme Court rejected that plan in September, upholding a federal judge’s order that temporarily blocked the U.S. Postal Service from moving forward with the new requirements for ballots.
Trump and some far-right congressional Republicans have also been pushing — unsuccessfully — to pass the SAVE America Act, a voter suppression bill that would require voters to present proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and ID before they can cast a ballot.
Senate Democrats launched the Senate Election Observer Program back in June, citing fears of exactly these kinds of attempts of interference. They now say they have trained more than 100 staffers since then.
“Donald Trump is trying to steal the election — but Democrats and the American people won’t let him,” Schumer said Wednesday, adding that he is “grateful for the Senate staff members who are raising their hand to help build trust in our upcoming election and protect the sanctity of our democracy.”
“The voters will decide the next election — not Trump,” the minority leader added.
The trained staffers will not interfere with election officials’ duties, Senate Democrats said. The program will simply place trained observers on the ground to document any election interference, including any potential instances of voter interference, threats to election workers, misinformation and disinformation as well as any issues that may come up regarding the certification of elections.

item.content:encoded:
Sen. Tim Scott introduces bipartisan BRIDGE act of 2026 to support military families
WASHINGTON (WCIV) — Sen. Tim Scott and Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., have introduced bipartisan legislation that would create a pilot program to assist service members and their families as they transition from military to civilian life.
The Building Readiness and Integration for Dependents Going to Civilian Environments, or BRIDGE Act of 2026, would establish a three-year Department of Defense pilot program at four military installations to provide community-based support and transition services.
The program would offer resources including peer support, spouse employment assistance, skills training, benefits navigation and individualized transition plans for service members within one year of separation and their families.
"South Carolina is blessed to be home to thousands of our nation's heroes," Scott said in a statement. "The men and women of the Armed Forces, and their families who have sacrificed alongside them, have earned the best possible support as they transition to civilian life."
Scott said the legislation is intended to connect military families with support systems in their local communities.
"The BRIDGE Act empowers local communities to provide military families with tailored assistance, because the best solutions are often built closest to home," he said.
READ MORE | Tim Scott introduces trio of bills on film production, critical minerals and birth tourism
Padilla highlighted the struggles military families in this space are currently facing.
“We must do more to ensure that military families have the support they need after they leave active duty," he said. "Our bipartisan BRIDGE Act would create a pilot program to help us prioritize programs that focus on bridging the gap in services for veterans and military families.”
The legislation would also require coordination between the Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs, prioritize service members facing involuntary or accelerated separations and track outcomes related to employment, financial stability and family well-being.
The bill has received endorsements from several veterans and military family organizations, including Blue Star Families, the Wounded Warrior Project, the American Legion, the National Military Family Association, the Veterans of Foreign Wars and the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors.
Blue Star Families CEO Kathy Roth-Douquet said the organization's 2025 Military Family Lifestyle Survey found that 58% of respondents described their transition from military to civilian life as "difficult" or "very difficult."
"The BRIDGE Act recognizes that successful transition requires personalized, whole-family support that helps families build long-term stability, resilience, and connection as they move into civilian life," Roth-Douquet said.

item.content:encoded:
Lawmakers’ brief urges Ninth Circuit to reverse district court’s decision, issue preliminary injunction
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), and Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), led an amicus brief to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in the case of California v. Wright, challenging the Trump administration’s illegal overreach to restart the Sable Offshore Oil Pipeline.
Last month, the lawmakers submitted a brief in this case to the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California explaining that the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to restart the Sable Offshore oil pipeline grossly misuses the statute’s national defense intent for a corporate rescue mission to bail out the Administration’s political allies. The U.S. District Court for the Central District of California ignored the evidence of pay-to-play corruption and allowed the pipeline to continue operating.
The lawmakers’ latest brief reasserts that the Administration’s DPA Order fails to justify invoking this extraordinary authority. “DOE relies on vague national defense justifications of questionable relevance for the Order but fails to articulate why Sable’s crude-oil production and operation … are ‘necessary’ for national defense …. The Order fails to identify any specific military need for crude oil or even explain how Sable’s crude will be refined and ultimately distributed for military use. …. Sable does not produce the type of refined products that the military purchases, and the Wright Order identifies no supply-chain mechanism that would ensure that Sable’s crude is ultimately used by the military.”
The Administration’s weak national defense justification “does not relieve a court of determining whether the Executive Branch has, in good faith, established the statutory prerequisites that Congress imposed on the exercise of national-defense judgments and associated statutory authority .… [The prerequisites] are safeguards that Congress deliberately built into Title I—and refined over decades—to confine extraordinary federal intervention into private enterprise to circumstances in which prioritization or allocation is objectively necessary for national defense.”
The Trump Administration has repeatedly invoked spurious national security or emergency justifications to favor fossil fuel production: halting offshore wind projects, exempting Gulf oil and gas activity from endangered species protections, exempting dozens of coal plants from pollution control requirements, and prohibiting planned coal pant retirements. This order to restart the Sable Offshore oil pipeline is the latest example of “an Administration hell-bent on expanding fossil-fuel production.” Moreover, the project was helmed by a Trump donor, raising the specter of pay-to-play politics; DOE “intervened to rescue a favored political ally from financial ruin and bypass the state-law obstacles that had kept its pipelines idle for nearly eleven years.”
The lawmakers concluded, “The district court erred by accepting DOE’s national-defense rationale at face value rather than testing it against the statutory prerequisites, the record, and publicly available information …. the Court should reverse the district court’s denial of the preliminary injunction.”
Joining Whitehouse, Padilla, Schiff, and Carbajal, the amicus brief is co-signed by Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and Representatives Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Nanette Díaz Barragán (D-CA-44), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), and Mike Thompson (D-CA-04).

item.content:encoded:
Johan Vásquez ha sido uno de los futbolistas mexicanos más regulares que juega en Europa. Asentado en el Genoa de Italia, el defensor se ganó la capitanía desde hace tiempo y se convirtió en un verdadero referente de su equipo. Además, tuvo un papel muy correcto con México en el Mundial 2026, motivos que han generado que un grande de España se fijara en él.
Según la información que compartió el diario AS, Mateu Alemany, director deportivo de Atlético de Madrid, tiene a Johan Vásquez como una de sus opciones para reforzar el sector defensivo del equipo. Si bien es cierto que aún no existe ninguna oferta formal, el equipo colchonero ha iniciado un seguimiento que podría transformarse en un ofrecimiento en el mercado de invierno.
El desafío que afrontaría Johan Vásquez si firma por Atlético de Madrid
En caso de llegar al Atlético de Madrid, el defensor mexicano daría un salto de calidad considerable. Sin embargo, llegaría a un equipo con jugadores de buen rendimiento en la última línea, por lo que debería competir arduamente para ganarse un puesto. Marc Pubill, Robin Le Normand, Cristian ‘Cuti’ Romero y Dávid Hancko son algunas de las alternativas más destacadas del entrenador Diego Simeone.
Lo cierto es que el Colchonero no tiene urgencia de reforzar su zaga central, aunque están evaluando posibilidades de mercado y Johan es una de ellas. Este interés se suma al de Juventus y el Eintracht Frankfurt, clubes que ya se mostraron atentos a su situación durante el mercado de verano. Sin embargo, la intención del Genoa es clara: quiere mantener a su capitán a toda costa.

¿Cuál es el valor de mercado de Johan Vásquez y hasta cuándo tiene contrato?
De acuerdo con Transfermarkt, Johan Vásquez tiene un valor de mercado de 14 millones de euros. Sin embargo, esta cifra es una estimación y no representa necesariamente el precio que pediría el Genoa para dejar salir a su capitán.
Por otro lado, el defensor mexicano tiene contrato hasta el 30 de junio de 2028. Su última renovación fue anunciada en septiembre de 2025, cuando el conjunto italiano aseguró la continuidad de uno de sus referentes.
Esto quiere decir que, al finalizar la temporada 2026-2027, a Johan le quedará solamente un año de vínculo. Ese escenario podría abrir la puerta a una negociación, aunque cualquier equipo interesado deberá llegar a un acuerdo con el Genoa para concretar su fichaje.

item.content:encoded:
La noche en el Memorial Coliseum de Los Ángeles dejó una postal inesperada para la Selección Mexicana: un equipo sin victorias en cuatro partidos, dos derrotas consecutivas y el debut de un joven arquero, Álex Padilla, bajo la atenta mirada de Rafael Márquez. El histórico exdefensor, ahora al mando del Tricolor, no tardó en mostrar que su etapa estará marcada por cambios profundos y decisiones firmes.
El marcador final ante Chile, un 2-0 que dolió más por la falta de reacción que por la diferencia, fue el punto de quiebre. Márquez, apodado el Káiser, fue claro en conferencia de prensa: "Hemos visto quién puede estar y quién no". Su mensaje fue directo, casi una advertencia: la Selección Mexicana entrará en una nueva fase, donde el rendimiento y la actitud serán determinantes para ganarse un lugar.
El debut de Álex Padilla y los ajustes en el once titular
Uno de los momentos más significativos de esta concentración fue el debut de Álex Padilla en la portería. El joven guardameta del Athletic de Bilbao, tras dos años de convocatorias, finalmente tuvo su oportunidad en un partido oficial. Márquez, fiel a su promesa de observar a todos los jugadores, también realizó cambios notables en la defensa y el ataque: Dagoberto Espinoza y Everardo López ingresaron en la zaga, mientras que Germán Berterame y Armando González lideraron la ofensiva.
La alineación titular ante Chile reflejó la búsqueda de Márquez por nuevas fórmulas. La portería estuvo resguardada por Padilla, acompañado en defensa por Espinoza, Israel Reyes, Jesús Gallardo y López. En el mediocampo, Erik Lira, Álvaro Fidalgo y Obed Vargas intentaron darle equilibrio al equipo, mientras que el ataque quedó en manos de Berterame, González y Roberto Alvarado.
Un balance negativo y la presión del banquillo
El saldo de la primera concentración de Márquez al frente del Tricolor fue duro: dos empates (ante Colombia y Perú) y dos derrotas (frente a Estados Unidos y Chile). El funcionamiento del equipo, según el propio entrenador, dejó dudas especialmente en defensa, donde "nos ganaron muy fácil las espaldas", y en ataque, donde las oportunidades fueron escasas y poco aprovechadas.
La presión sobre Márquez es evidente. Tomó el relevo de Javier Aguirre con la expectativa de renovar el proyecto deportivo rumbo al Mundial 2030, pero los resultados iniciales han encendido las alarmas. El propio técnico reconoce que el principal objetivo de esta etapa fue "darle minutos a todos" y conocer de cerca a los jugadores, especialmente a los más jóvenes y a quienes vienen trabajando con él desde la pasada Copa del Mundo.
El mensaje de Márquez: oportunidades y exigencia
"Te das cuenta de que le diste oportunidad a todos, minutos y desde un principio se presupuestó para intentarlos ver, era el principal objetivo. Hemos visto quién puede estar y quién no", insistió Márquez tras la derrota ante Chile. Su enfoque, más que preocuparse, es ocuparse: buscar que los futbolistas tengan ritmo de competencia y sumar a los que están en Europa para fortalecer al grupo.
Las decisiones no se harán esperar. De cara a la próxima convocatoria para la Nations League, donde México enfrentará a Jamaica en los cuartos de final, se esperan varios movimientos clave. Nombres como Raúl Jiménez, Julián Quiñones, Edson Álvarez y César Montes suenan como posibles incorporaciones para revertir la inercia negativa.
Un nuevo ciclo en marcha
La gestión de Márquez está apenas en sus primeros pasos, pero la exigencia es máxima. El recuerdo de otros técnicos que tardaron en conseguir su primera victoria, como Raúl Cárdenas en 1980, sirve de consuelo histórico, pero la presión mediática y de la afición es otra en estos tiempos.
México volverá a la acción a mediados de noviembre, con la obligación de mostrar una cara diferente y, sobre todo, resultados. La era de Rafael Márquez ha comenzado entre ajustes, oportunidades y la promesa de una renovación profunda. El Tricolor, sacudido por los cambios, busca reencontrar su identidad y volver a ilusionar a su gente.

item.content:encoded:
Alex Padilla salió en defensa del proceso encabezado por Rafael Márquez después de la derrota de la Selección Mexicana por 0-2 ante Chile, resultado que dejó al combinado nacional sin victorias durante los cuatro partidos de la Fecha FIFA.
El guardameta, quien recibió la oportunidad de debutar como titular ante los chilenos, reconoció que los errores cometidos por México terminaron siendo determinantes, pero pidió al grupo mantener la autocrítica y rescatar los aspectos positivos mostrados durante estos encuentros.
En declaraciones para TUDN, Padilla aseguró que el plantel mantiene la confianza en el proceso de Rafael Márquez y consideró que los resultados no reflejan por completo el funcionamiento que tuvo el equipo en distintos momentos.
“Lo que no podemos hacer es quedarnos en el resultado, es lo que nos ha llevado al resultado; somos los primeros que confiamos en el proceso, se palpa. Los errores nos han penalizado en goles, de eso se trata; pero de lo malo, intentar sacar lo positivo y ser autocríticos”, señaló.
El arquero agregó que el balance de los cuatro encuentros no representa todo lo que México consiguió mostrar sobre el terreno de juego.
“Estos resultados no reflejan el buen futbol que hemos dado a ratos”, afirmó.
Más allá de los resultados, el portero también destacó el compromiso que existe dentro del vestidor y aseguró que los jugadores están dispuestos a continuar trabajando para corregir los errores.
Padilla consideró que México cuenta con un grupo unido y comprometido con el proceso, aunque reconoció que las equivocaciones han tenido un costo demasiado alto en los marcadores.
“Me deja tranquilo el compromiso del equipo, lo que siento que están dispuestos a luchar mis compañeros, somos un grupo unido; los errores nos penalizaron muy caro y debemos darle la vuelta cuanto antes”, indicó.
El encuentro ante Chile también representó el debut de Padilla con la Selección Mexicana. Rafael Márquez decidió darle la titularidad después de que Raúl ‘Tala’ Rangel estuviera bajo los reflectores tras sus errores en la derrota por 0-3 ante Estados Unidos.
La derrota ante Chile cerró una Fecha FIFA complicada para el conjunto mexicano, que terminó con dos empates y dos derrotas.
El equipo nacional igualó 1-1 ante Colombia y 1-1 frente a Perú, antes de caer 0-3 contra Estados Unidos y finalmente perder 0-2 ante Chile.
Ante los chilenos, México tuvo dificultades para reaccionar en el segundo tiempo. Al minuto 54, Maxi Gutiérrez recibió un pase filtrado y aprovechó una falla defensiva para superar a Padilla y poner el 1-0.
Posteriormente, al 65’, Chile volvió a aprovechar una pérdida de balón del conjunto mexicano. Vicente Pizarro recibió un pase filtrado y, tras quedar sin marca, definió cruzado para establecer el 2-0 definitivo.
Rafael Márquez realizó cinco modificaciones después del primer tanto chileno, pero México no logró encontrar una respuesta suficiente para evitar una nueva derrota.

Seleção de Rafa Márquez termina estágio sem vitórias e com apenas dois golos marcados em quatro jogos
Foram duas semanas para esquecer para a seleção do México e para Santiago Gimenez, avançado do FC Porto. A expectativa criada por um bom Mundial (quatro vitórias nos quatro primeiros jogos), pese a eliminação nos oitavos de final (contra Inglaterra), deu lugar à frustração de quatro jogos sem qualquer triunfo.
Na última madrugada, em Los Angeles, perante 56539 espectadores, a seleção mexicana voltou a perder, 0-2 com o Chile, num encontro que pôs a nu as muitas lacunas da tentativa de renovação levada a cabo pelo novo selecionador Rafa Márquez.
A partida ficou ainda marcada pela homenagem prévia prestada a Guillermo Ochoa, histórico guarda-redes que passou pelo Aves SAD, sob o lema Thank You Memo, e pela estreia a titular de Alex Padilla na baliza mexicana. Apesar das várias alterações promovidas por Rafa Márquez na tentativa de encontrar soluções, o conjunto mexicano voltou a evidenciar falta de clareza e de ligação entre os seus elementos do ataque, o que gerou a crescente impaciência dos adeptos nas bancadas ao longo do encontro.
A eficácia chilena acabou por resolver a partida no segundo tempo. Aos 56 minutos, Maximiliano Gutiérrez inaugurou o marcador após assistência de Gonzalo Tapia, que recuperou a posse de bola no meio-campo e deu início à jogada concluída no interior da área adversária.
Oito minutos depois, o selecionador mexicano lançou Santiago Gimenez para o lugar de Armando González, que desiludiu como titular na posição de ponta de lança (e fez mais quatro substituições), e... 55 segundos depois o Chile fez o 2-0, numa jogada em que Johan Vásquez, acabado de entrar, ficou caído no relvado, e que Vicente Pizarro concluiu a passe de Darío Osorio.
O México ainda carregou para tentar reduzir, mas quase não criou oportunidades. Santiago Gimenez fez apenas um remate, disparatado, aos 83' e a seleção termina esta série de jogos em datas FIFA com dois empates (Colômbia e Peru) e duas derrotas (Estados Unidos e Chile, que tinha sido a pior seleção sul-americana na qualificação para o Mundial, com duas vitórias em 18 jornadas), dois golos marcados e sete sofridos.
Rafa Márquez, em todo o caso, desvalorizou a série de maus resultados. «Não se pode comparar um Mundial com jogos particulares. O principal objetivo era ver jogadores e dar minutos a todos. Deu para perceber quem pode estar e quem não pode. Neste jogo faltou-nos contundência nas duas áreas, mas eram miúdos que estavam a jogar juntos pela primeira vez», assinalou.

Álex Padilla aseguró que hay plena confianza en el proceso de Rafael Márquez luego de la derrota de la Selección Mexicana frente a Chile para cerrar la fecha FIFA sin conocer la victoria tras cuatro juegos disputados.
El arquero señaló que los errores que tuvieron les han costado caro, pero tendrán que ser muy autocríticos con lo demostrado.
“Lo que no podemos hacer es quedarnos en el resultado, es lo que nos ha llevado al resultad o, somos los primeros que confiamos en el proceso, se palpa, los errores nos han penalizado en goles, de eso se trata, pero de lo malo, intentar sacar lo positivo y ser autocríticos"
"Me deja tranquilo el compromiso del equipo, lo que siento que están dispuestos a luchar mis compañeros, somos un grupo unido, estos resultados no reflejan el buen futbol que hemos dado a ratos, los errores nos penalizaron muy caro y debemos darle la vuelta cuanto antes", indicó Álex Padilla.
Álex Padilla debutó como portero de la Selección Mexicana al ser elegido por Rafael Márquez como el titular en el juego ante Chile luego de presenciar los primer juegos desde el banquillo.

La Selección Mexicana tenía este partido ante Chile para romper esa mala racha de partidos sin ganar en la Fecha FIFA. El equipo de Rafael Márquez tuvo cuatro oportunidades para ello y en todas falló. Pero en este duelo, ante el rival que había sido exhibido ante Estados Unidos, la oportunidad de vencer era más fuerte, pero no se pudo.
México ya iba perdiendo 1-0, por lo que el estratega decidió hacer cambios, entre los jugadores que recién ingresaban estaba Johan Vásquez a quien no había intención de meter en este duelo, pero ante las necesidades en la central decidió utilizarlo, apenas tenía un minuto en el terreno de juego cuando un error suyo provocó la segunda anotación de los chilenos.
¡El oso de Johan Vásquez!
Fue en el minuto 65 del encuentro cuando Darío Osorio filtra el balón para cederlo a su compañero que estaba en el área, ahí es cuando Johan se barre pero el balón no se detuvo y se filtró la pelota hacia Vicente Pizarro quien ya sólo se acomoda el balón y consigue rematar de pierna izquierda venciendo a Alex Padilla en el arco.
SE LE FUE A VÁZQUEZ Y CHILE MARCÓ EL SEGUNDO 🇨🇱 Johan Vázquez tenía segundos en el juego cuando midió mal un balón que le permitió a Vicente Pizarro ingresar al área para definir frente al arco de Padilla. 📹: Clarosports https://t.co/AY3mbgFrx3
— ONCE Diario (@oncediariomx) October 7, 2026
De esta manera cayó el segundo tanto que ponía las cosas más complicadas para el equipo mexicano después de que hubiera hecho cinco cambios de golpe. En los 20 minutos restantes fue poco lo que Rafa le pudo mover al plantel, pero no consiguieron ninguna anotación para poder por lo menos igualar en el marcador, por lo que terminan con su segunda derrota y dos empates.
En síntesis
- Johan Vásquez provocó el segundo gol de Chile al minuto de ingresar.
- Vicente Pizarro marcó el 2-0 al minuto 65 venciendo a Alex Padilla.
- Rafael Márquez suma dos derrotas y dos empates con la Selección Mexicana.

De acuerdo con fuentes cercanas al campamento nacional, el director técnico Rafa Márquez cumplirá su palabra y mantendrá el plan original estipulado para esta ventana internacional, confirmando que Alex Padilla titular con México será la apuesta bajo los tres palos en el Memorial Coliseum.
A continuación, en 365Scores te detallamos los motivos de la decisión, la alineación en el arco y la antesala del choque donde Alex Padilla titular con México acapara la atención.
Rafa Márquez cumple su plan en la portería
Aunque tras la dura derrota ante Estados Unidos en Arizona circularon versiones sobre un posible espaldarazo inmediato a Raúl “Tala” Rangel para resarcirse de sus errores, el cuerpo técnico prefirió no alterar la hoja de ruta establecida desde el inicio del MexTour. La determinación de ver a Alex Padilla titular con México responde a la distribución de minutos que el “Káiser” tenía presupuestada para evaluar a sus arqueros.
El guardameta del Athletic Club saltará al terreno de juego como inicialista, asumiendo la responsabilidad de darle solidez al bloque defensivo en el compromiso México vs Chile.
La oportunidad de oro para el guardameta
El choque de esta noche ante el conjunto andino representa una prueba de fuego para la zaga tricolor. Con la confirmación de Alex Padilla titular con México, el juvenil buscará aprovechar la vitrina internacional para afianzarse dentro de la competencia interna en la portería azteca de cara a las próximas citas oficiales de la Concacaf.
La presencia de Alex Padilla titular con México genera alta expectativa entre la afición que se dará cita en el escenario de Los Ángeles para el cierre de la fecha FIFA.
Horario del compromiso México vs Chile
El encuentro internacional entre México vs Chile arrancará a las 20:30 horas (Tiempo del Centro de México) en el Memorial Coliseum. La transmisión en directo estará disponible en televisión abierta por Canal 5 y Azteca 7, así como en TUDN y la plataforma Amazon Prime Video.

México cerrará esta noche la Fecha FIFA ante Chile y ya hay especulaciones sobre la alineación que Rafa Márquez prepara. Uno de los dilemas está en la portería y es que hay dudas sobre si usará al Tala Rangel o Álex Padilla.
Mucho se ha especulado sobre quién tomará la portería para el último partido de la Fecha FIFA, luego de los errores del guardameta de Chivas en la derrota frente a Estados Unidos del sábado pasado. Ante esto, el entrenador del Tri mostró su respaldo y confianza hacia Tala, pero podría darle oportunidad a un elemento diferente.
De los porteros de México en esta Fecha FIFA, Rangel y Oscar García han sumado minutos, por lo que Padilla falta de tener oportunidad y en este partido frente a Chile pinta para ser titular y así completar la rotación de encuentros. Te contamos cómo sería la alineación del Tri.
Álex Padilla sería titular en el México vs Chile
En medio de las bajas que ha tenido México para su enfrentamiento ante Chile, Rafa Márquez tuvo que modificar su alineación en la defensa y mediocampo. A estos cambios también se le añadiría la titularidad de Álex Padilla, quien tendrá la oportunidad de mostrarse.
